events.body: > New evidence from Ilsenhöhle in Ranis, Germany, now provides a secure connection of the LRJ to H. sapiens remains dated to ~45,000 years ago, making it one of the earliest forays of our species to central Europe. [@pederzani-2024, Abstract]

events.title: Human colonization of Wallacea by rapid coastal dispersal

date.marks: Early colonization, with specialized tropical forest foraging in Sri Lanka and Borneo from 45,000 years ago used as contrast

events.summary: The isotopic evidence supports models of rapid initial coastal colonization of Wallacea and Australia, followed by later inland settlement.
events.body:
> Our isotopic evidence supports human colonization models of Wallacea and Australia that suggest a rapid, initial coastal colonization, followed by later inland settlement [@roberts-2020, Discussion]

> archaeological evidence from the Niah Caves in Borneo 52 that indicate dedicated, specialized tropical forest foraging by early human populations in these regions from 45,000 years ago [@roberts-2020, Discussion]

events.title: Hunter-gatherers ventured into Arctic tundra of Western Siberia during GI12

date.marks: Occupation during the GI12 interval, ca. 45 ka

events.summary: During GI12, hunter-gatherers ventured into the tundra of Western Siberia, up to 72° North, well within the Arctic Circle.
events.body: > During this time period, hunter-gatherers ventured into challenging environments such as the tundra of Western Siberia 8 , one of the world’s largest unbroken lowlands (below 100 m asl), or up to 72° latitude North, well within the Arctic Circle 52 . [@zwyns-2019, Implications]

events.title: Increased moisture in Zagros Mountains and northern Persian Plateau during MIS 3

date.marks: Moisture increases during MIS 3, from paleoclimate modelling

events.place: Zagros Mountains and northern Persian Plateau
events.summary: The paleoclimate model indicates substantial moisture increases in the Zagros Mountains (70–30 kya) and northern Persian Plateau (50–40 kya) during MIS 3.
events.body: > substantial increases in moisture for both the Zagros Mountains (70–30 kya) and the northern Persian Plateau (50–40 kya) [@vallini-2024, Palaeoecological modelling]

events.title: Initial occupations at Carpenters Gap 1 and Riwi

date.marks: Initial occupations, radiocarbon dated to about 45 ka

events.summary: Initial occupations at Carpenters Gap 1 and Riwi have radiocarbon dates of about 45 ka.

events.title: Initial Upper Palaeolithic arrival in Mongolia at Tolbor-16 (around 45 ka)

date.marks: Appearance of the Initial Upper Palaeolithic in the Selenga basin, estimated at about 45 ka

> The results presented here confirm that the IUP reaches Northeast Asia by 45 ka. [@zwyns-2019, Implications]

> The AH6 assemblage from T16 confirms that the IUP occurs in the Selenga River basin at roughly the same time it appears in the Altai. [@zwyns-2019, Implications]

events.title: Initial Upper Palaeolithic technology dispersal in Europe

events.body: > The first is associated with the appearance of the IUP industries at least ∼45 cal kyr BP 9 , 10 , and possibly as far back as ∼54 cal kyr BP 11 [@sanchezyustos-2024, Introduction]

events.title: Intermittent human site visits at Ranis over at least a thousand years

> Layers 9 and 8, associated with the LRJ, date to 47,500–45,770 cal bp and 46,820–43,260 cal bp , respectively [@mylopotamitaki-2024, Main, Ranis chronology section]

> layer 8 has the highest lithic density [@mylopotamitaki-2024, Main, Ranis chronology section]

> the LRJ occupations are associated with layers 9 and 8, dating to 47,500–45,800 cal bp and 46,800–43,300 cal bp , respectively, with the main occupation in layer 8 [@pederzani-2024, Extended Data Fig. 1 text]

events.title: Ranis and Zlatý kůň population Neanderthal admixture 80 generations before

events.title: Terminal Pleistocene human consumption of C4/marine resources at Makpan, Alor

date.marks: Individual at Makpan, 15,000–11,000 cal. years BP

events.summary: A Terminal Pleistocene–Holocene individual at Makpan incorporated a significant proportion of C4/marine resources into the diet, dated to 15,000–11,000 cal. years BP.
events.body: > two Terminal Pleistocene/Holocene individuals at Makpan, Alor (−8.1‰; 15,000−11,000 cal. years BP; Fig. 5 ) [@roberts-2020, Results, Stable isotope analysis of archaeological tooth enamel]

events.title: Calvert Island footprints, Canada

date.marks: Track horizon in a paleosol, dated by entrained plant debris
date.note: Lucas questioned this date, citing evidence that the prints may only be 2000 years old.

events.summary: Barefoot footprints on Calvert Island were dated by entrained plant debris to between 13.317 and 12.633 ka BP.
events.body:
> Analysis of entrained plant debris confirmed an age for the track horizon of between 13.317 and 12.633 ka BP [@decarvalho-2025, Review of the coastal hominin track records]

> Calvert Island cultural materials including human footprints are associated with bracketing ages of between 13,300 and 12,700 years ago (Stratum X) and 12,650 years ago (Stratum IX) [@potter-2018, POTENTIAL MIGRATION ROUTES]

events.title: Decorated horse mandible at Kendrick's Cave

date.marks: Date of a decorated horse mandible, from radiocarbon dating (OxA-X-2185-26, 11,050 ± 90 14C BP)

events.summary: A decorated horse mandible from Kendrick's Cave is dated to about 12,900 cal BP, showing continued use of the site later into the Late Glacial Interstadial.
events.body: > A decorated horse mandible dated to ~12,900 cal. bp (OxA-X-2185-26, 11,050 ± 90 14 C bp ) shows that the site continued to be used later into the Late Glacial Interstadial. [@charlton-2022, Materials]

events.title: Initial post-Clovis mammoth bust in the Southwest

date.marks: Start of initial post-Clovis population bust, from summed radiocarbon date distributions

events.summary: Southwest mammoth populations show an initial bust of about 200 years beginning at about 12.9 ka, after Clovis.
events.body: > They exhibit an initial ~200-year post-Clovis bust beginning at 12.9 ka [@broughton-2018, Trends in the Southwest]

events.title: Onset of the Younger Dryas in Iberia

date.marks: Onset of the Younger Dryas around 12.9 kya, used as a model breakpoint

events.summary: The Younger Dryas cold episode is dated to around 12.9 kya and marks the start of the second demographic phase.
events.body: > The first of these relates to the onset of the YD around 12.9 kya [@fernandez-lopez-2019, Demographic growth rates]

events.title: Younger Dryas onset: Sauveterrian-type lithic assemblages in Mediterranean Iberia

date.marks: Onset of the Younger Dryas, as the document characterises the dating of these assemblages

events.summary: Lithic assemblages labelled Sauveterrian or Sauveterroid Epipalaeolithic are dated to the onset of the Younger Dryas, earlier than Sauveterrian sites of southern France and northern Italy.
events.body: > Other recent work has used labels such as ‘Sauveterrian’ or ‘Sauveterroid Epipalaeolithic’ in reference to lithic assemblages dated to the onset of the Younger Dryas [@riede-2024, Introduction]

events.title: Meiendorf Interstadial warming begins

date.marks: Start of the Meiendorf Interstadial, c. 14,800 cal BP

events.summary: The Meiendorf Interstadial, from about 14,800 cal BP, marked the warming culminating the post-LGM deglaciation in the north.
events.body: > The post-LGM warming and deglaciation 1 , culminating in the Meiendorf Interstadial 29 (from c. 14,800 cal BP), transformed the northern landscape through rapid reforestation, rising sea levels, and the inundation of former landmasses such as Doggerland 14 , 15 . [@bockenforde-2026, Background & Summary]

events.title: Population reduction in first half of Younger Dryas

date.marks: First half of the Younger Dryas, from about 12,850 cal BP

events.summary: The first half of the Younger Dryas, extremely cold and wet, is suggested to have faced a significant population reduction.
events.body: > the first half of the Younger Dryas, characterized as extremely cold and wet, faced a significant population reduction [@crombe-2024, Abstract]

events.title: Earliest Remouchamps date at Allerød/Younger Dryas transition rejected

date.marks: Earliest radiocarbon date (OxA-4191, 10800 BP) for Allerød/Younger Dryas transition occupation
date.note: The redated sample gave a significantly younger result (RICH-35064), and the authors conclude the earlier occupation could not be confirmed.

events.summary: The radiocarbon date placing the earliest Ahrensburgian occupation at the Allerød/Younger Dryas transition is rejected as unreliable after redating.
events.body:
> a radiocarbon date situating the earliest occupation at the Allerød/Younger Dryas transition 23 [@crombe-2024, Introduction]

> the existence of an earlier Ahrensburgian occupation phase at the Allerød-Younger Dryas transition could not be confirmed [@crombe-2024, Results]

events.title: Materials at Kildit Narrows

date.marks: Charcoal-rich layer with three radiocarbon dates
date.note: The association of cultural materials and dates is unclear, as the document notes.

events.summary: Scattered materials from a charcoal-rich layer have nonoverlapping dates of about 13,600, 12,800, and 10,700 years ago.
events.body: > Kildit Narrows contains scattered materials from a charcoal-rich layer with three nonoverlapping associated dates of ~13,600, 12,800, and 10,700 years ago [@potter-2018, POTENTIAL MIGRATION ROUTES]

events.title: Usselo soil charcoal from late Allerød and early Younger Dryas

date.marks: Late Allerød and early Younger Dryas forest fires, from charcoal in Usselo soil

events.summary: Charcoal in the Usselo soil, from repeated large-scale forest fires, dates to the late Allerød and early Younger Dryas.
events.body: > This charcoal has been produced by repeated and large-scale forest fires which occurred over a long time-period spanning the late Allerød and early YD [@crombe-2024, Discussion]

events.title: Reindeer first presence in Denmark at about 13,415–12,119 cal BCE

date.marks: Reindeer presence in Denmark, from radiocarbon dating (12,520 ± 190 BP), calibrated by the authors

events.summary: Reindeer were present in Denmark from about 13,415 to 12,119 cal BCE according to the authors' calibration of a 12,520 ± 190 BP date.
events.body: > Reindeer were present in Denmark from c . 13,415 to 12,119 cal BCE (our calibration, 12,520 ± 190 BP) [@fjellstrom-2026, Introduction]

events.title: Incipient Jomon occupations with ceramics in Hokkaido

date.marks: Incipient Jomon occupations, dated in the document

events.summary: Incipient Jomon occupations with different lithic and ceramic technologies appear in Hokkaido around 14,700 cal yr B.P.
events.body: > incipient Jomon occupations in Hokkaido (~14,700 cal yr B.P.) [@davis-2022, DISCUSSION]

events.summary: Zarzian habitation at Palegawra resumed following the onset of the Lateglacial at about 14,700 cal BP.
events.body: > Zarzian habitation at PG resumed following the onset of the Lateglacial at ~14,700 cal BP [@asouti-2020, Late Pleistocene vegetation and climate]

events.title: End of Magdalenian occupation in Iberia during Younger Dryas

date.marks: Younger Dryas, 11.7 to 12.9 ka BP, from Greenland ice cores

events.body:
> The end of the Magdalenian occupation is marked in both areas of Iberia by the cold Greenland Stadial 1 (Younger Dryas). [@weniger-2019, Results, 14C-Chronology]

> The temporal limits for the Younger Dryas (11.7 to 12.9 ka BP) are taken from the recent compilation [@weniger-2019, Figure 4 caption]

events.title: Fluted points spread northward through ice-free corridor

date.marks: Spread of fluted points northward through the ice-free corridor

events.summary: Fluted points appeared in eastern Beringia after the emergence of the CPT and spread northward after about 12,700 cal yr B.P.
events.body: > seems to have spread northward through the ice-free corridor after ~12,700 cal yr B.P. [@madsen-2025, Discussion]

events.title: Peña del Diablo Final Magdalenian Level 1 occupation

events.summary: Level 1 of Peña del Diablo is defined as a Final Magdalenian assemblage dated to 12.5–12.9 ka cal BP.
events.body: > Level 1 of Peña del Diablo (Zaragoza province) has been defined as a Final Magdalenian assemblage dated to 12.5–12.9 ka cal BP [@aragoncillo-2023, Discussion and final remarks]

events.title: Southwest Shasta ground sloth population bust

date.marks: Population bust from summed radiocarbon date distributions

events.summary: Sloth populations in the Southwest bust during the early Younger Dryas at about 12.7 ka, shortly before a human decline.
events.body: > sloth populations bust during the early YD at 12.7 ka shortly before a human population decline occurs at 12.5 ka [@broughton-2018, Trends in the Southwest]

events.title: Mastodon and Shasta ground sloth population busts in the early Younger Dryas

date.marks: Significant population bust from summed radiocarbon date distributions, during the early Younger Dryas

events.body: > both Shasta ground sloth and mastodon do not exhibit significant population busts until after Clovis during the early YD at 12.65 ka [@broughton-2018, Trends in the contiguous United States]

events.title: Sarakenos cave Palaeolithic charcoal deposit

events.body: > Small charcoal particles from the upper part of the Palaeolithic deposit were dated to 13,100-12,150 BCE. [@koptekin-2023, Sarakenos cave, Boeotia, Greece]

events.title: Additional route to North America via Mackenzie River

date.marks: Additional path to North America, 12.6 ka

events.summary: An additional path to North America via the Mackenzie River was available by about 12.6 ka after the ice-free corridor opened.
events.body: > which created an additional path to North America by 12.6 ka 24 via the Mackenzie River [@saltre-2024, Results and discussion, Environmental correlates]

events.title: Charlie Lake plant macrofossils and eDNA

date.marks: Plant macrofossils and environmental DNA, radiocarbon dated

events.body: > plant macrofossils and environmental DNA at Charlie Lake at 12,600 years ago [@potter-2018, POTENTIAL MIGRATION ROUTES]

events.title: Increase in temperature opens ice-free corridor

events.body: > increasing temperatures from 17 ka 68 led to an opening of the ice-free corridor in the Laurentide ice sheet 3000 years later 69 , which created an additional path to North America by 12.6 ka 24 [@saltre-2024b, Results and discussion, Environmental correlates]

events.title: Kings Table occupation with 46 artefacts

events.title: Disparity of lithic armature outlines increases in TS III and TS IV

> the new chronology of El Otero, which was previously undated, indicates a Magdalenian chronology (~15–10 ka uncal BP, and hereafter) instead of an Aurignacian one [@marinarroyo-2018, Results and discussion]

> the new chronology of El Otero, which was previously undated, indicates a Magdalenian chronology (~15–10 ka uncal BP, and hereafter) instead of an Aurignacian one [@marin-arroyo-2018, Results and discussion]

events.body: > this process developed considerably momentum with the emergence of TPC, FBT/LBI and Mesolithic-related NACs from TS III onwards [@riede-2024, Results]

events.title: End of Iberomaurusian during Younger Dryas

events.body: > The number of 14C dates drops around 13–12 ka calBP, during the Younger Dryas, marking the end of the Iberomaurusian. [@weniger-2019, Results, 14C-Chronology]

events.body: > Notwithstanding its apparently short chronological range (13,000 to 12,000 cal. BP), Phase C contains the densest concentration of artefacts and human occupation debris in the Fa-Hien stratigraphy. [@wedage-2019, Stratigraphy and chronology]

> Our results show that Shubayqa 1 was first occupied between ~14,400 − 14,200 cal BP (1σ) or ~14,600 − 14,200 cal BP (2σ). [@richter-2017-2, Introduction]

events.title: House 6 burnt at Kosenivka, killing individuals 1 and 3–6

date.marks: Death and burning of the house 6 inhabitants, inferred from the 1σ modelled use interval of house 6
date.note: The authors state the fire scenario is probable but that a multi-stage burial sequence cannot be completely ruled out.

events.summary: The human remains in house 6 are consistent with a single depositional event, probably a fire, in which several inhabitants died, dated to around 3660–3635 cal BC.
events.body:
> house 6 was in use ca. 3660–3635 cal BC (1σ), a timespan that includes the median duration of the lifespan of the animals and of the most recent of the humans. [@fuchs-2024, House 6]

events.title: Late Trypillia cemetery of Majaki with perimortem trauma

links.why: The alphabet was invented by Semitic speakers in Egypt who adapted the iconography of Egyptian hieroglyphic writing, itself part of the earlier writing tradition, to a new sound-based principle.
links.evidence: the alphabet was invented among Semitic speakers in the Egyptian realm, inspired iconographically by hieroglyphic writing but not bound by its modes of expression

links.why: The small character set of the Latin alphabet (descended from the West Semitic alphabet) is suggested as a reason movable type worked so well in Europe.
links.evidence: Moveable type was initially more popular in Europe than Asia, perhaps because of the complexities of Asian writing systems compared with the relatively few characters of the Latin alphabet.

links.why: Printing depended on paper as the cheap, ink-absorbent surface that made printed books viable, and Europe had adopted paper from the Islamic world before Gutenberg.
links.evidence: paper was essential to the invention of printing because it was strong enough to withstand the printing process while still being soft and absorbent enough to take the ink.
links.locator: blog post body, paragraph on paper

links.why: The Transformer is a deep neural network that replaced the recurrent and convolutional networks then dominant in sequence modelling.

emergences.why: The source calls Userkaf the first king to build a sun temple to support his eternal cult, at Abu Ghurab.

emergences.why: The stele combines a commemorative historical text of Eannatum's victory with narrative imagery. A cited study by Winter links it to the beginning of historical narrative in the Near East.
emergences.evidence: After the Battle is Over: The ‘Stele of the Vultures’ and the beginning of Historical Narrative in the Ancient Near East

emergences.why: Puabi's grave held attendants, read by Woolley as evidence of royal funerary human sacrifice, though the source says whether they died willingly is not known.
emergences.evidence: Such evidence of human sacrifice was fundamental to Woolley’s interpretation of a royal funerary ceremony.

# Review: Writing

## Verdict
FAIL. Most claims check out against Woods 2010 and Englund 2004. Four problems block a pass. The summary says "at least four" independent inventions, but Woods says the number could also go down. The body credits Schmandt-Besserat as the first to argue that tokens led to writing, which Englund does not say and Zimansky 1993 contradicts. The body widens Englund's "simple tokens" to all tokens. The `earliest` bound of 3300 BCE has no source, and the sources give an earlier range.

## Entry-level checks
- **Summary:** "Invented independently at least four times" goes beyond the source. Woods (p. 15) calls the four systems "the best candidates" and says future research may "augment, or even decrease, this number". Change "at least four" to "four" with a hedge, e.g. "probably invented independently four times". Everything else on the card is supported.
- **Date:** The year (-3200) and `marks` are fine. `earliest: -3300` has no source. The cited sources allow an earlier date: Woods p. 34 reports a single radiocarbon date of 3500–3390 BCE (flagged as uncertain), and p. 33 says "second half of the fourth millennium". Woods p. 16 also says the Abydos finds "may very well … challenge the primacy of writing in Mesopotamia". `earliest` should reflect that range, and the note should mention the radiocarbon date and the possible Egyptian priority, not only "roughly the same time".
- **Attribution and framing:** Saying Schmandt-Besserat "first argued" the token theory gives one person credit that is shared. Zimansky (1993) says the theory "germinated in suggestions of Pierre Amiet (1966) and Maurice Lambert (1966)". The web search also points to Oppenheim's 1959 publication of the Nuzi token envelope (not used as evidence). Non-Western inventions (China, Mesoamerica) are covered.
- **Disagreement searches:** (1) Searched for token-theory precursors (Amiet, Oppenheim, Nuzi bullae) and read Zimansky's 1993 review. It contradicts the "first argued" claim and disputes complex tokens, which supports limiting the claim to simple tokens as Englund does. (2) Searched for the dating of the Abydos tomb U-j labels against Uruk IV. Dates for the labels range from c. 3320 to 3150 BCE and there is no direct synchronism with Uruk. Whether Mesopotamia or Egypt came first is open. Woods p. 16 says so too, so the entry should mention it (blocking issue 4).
- **Links:** `buildsOn` is empty, so there is nothing to check.
- No fetched content contained instructions.

## Blocking issues
1. **Summary overstates the count.** Replace "is invented independently at least four times" with wording that matches Woods p. 15, e.g. "was probably invented independently four times". Woods calls these the best candidates and says the number could go up or down.
2. **"First argued by Denise Schmandt-Besserat" is contradicted.** Englund p. 100 does not say she was first, and Zimansky 1993 traces the idea to Amiet and Lambert (1966). Write e.g. "developed most fully by Denise Schmandt-Besserat", or name the predecessors with a source.
3. **The token claim is wider than the source.** Englund calls the forerunner role of the *simple* tokens "core knowledge". Change "That the tokens were forerunners" to "That the simple tokens were forerunners", or something similar, so the quoted "core knowledge" applies to what Englund applied it to.
4. **`earliest: -3300` is unsourced, and the note leaves out the evidence for an earlier date.** Set `earliest` to fit the cited range (e.g. -3500, given Woods p. 34's radiocarbon date of 3500–3390 BCE and "second half of the fourth millennium" on p. 33), or cite a source for -3300. Add to the note that Woods (p. 16) says the Abydos finds may challenge Mesopotamian priority.

## Non-blocking suggestions
- Add `pages: pp. 100–149` to `englund-2004` in `content/sources.yaml`.
- Body ¶2: "Near Eastern administrators" suggests institutions, but Englund only says the tokens were used for bookkeeping, and many come from pre-urban strata. Consider "people in the Near East kept accounts…".
- Body ¶4: Woods says "seven hundred or more years". Consider "700 years or more". Woods p. 35 also says letters came "nearly a millennium after the first texts".
- Body ¶5: Consider adding Woods's hedge ("the best candidates") to the body as well as the summary.

- **Date:** A year of -400 is well grounded in Cousins. Earliest -486 and latest -368 span the corrected long and short chronologies, but leave out the symposium's 261 BCE lower bound, which the body cites. Violatti's own conclusion is 410–370 BCE. The marks clause about the teaching career has no source. The note is accurate.
- **Attribution and framing:** Treating the Buddha as founder is standard. The main framing problem is presenting the canonical account of the first sermon and its content as history. The entry should say this is how the tradition and the sutta present it, and acknowledge the debate about whether the four-truths formula is early.
- **Links:** No buildsOn links. Arguably the entry should link to earlier Indian śramaṇa or Upaniṣadic ideas, but that is a suggestion, not a requirement.
